The implementation is complete and verified. Here's the report.

## Your bookmarks app is built and ready to review — **http://maker:4000**

I built it fresh from the behaviours we approved together (not from the exploration prototype), as a real web app you can use.

### Verification outcome — all passing
- **12 end-to-end acceptance tests**, each mapped to the behaviours you approved, covering: saving with auto-fill, rejecting non-addresses, duplicate handling, the full search query language, read-later vs. reference and the tabs, archive/restore, permanent delete with confirmation, bulk actions (including whole-view select), sorting, Markdown notes, saved searches, import/export, display preferences, and the title-opens-original behaviour. **All 12 pass.**
- **16 unit tests** on the core logic (address validation & duplicate matching, the search query language, Markdown rendering, page-metadata extraction, and the standard import/export format). **All 16 pass.**

### What's in it — the scope you approved (25 scenarios)
Everything we settled: effortless saving with auto-filled title/description/icon/preview and tag suggestions; powerful finding (live search, `#tag`/AND/OR/NOT/`"phrases"`, click-a-tag, note excerpts, saved searches); read-later vs. finished with tabs; delete vs. reversible archive; bulk actions; sorting; Markdown notes; automatic preserved copies (page or PDF by real file type) with retry and optional Internet Archive; standard import/export; and display preferences.

### One honest note about the review environment
Fetching live page details, capturing preserved copies, and submitting to the Internet Archive all need outbound internet. If this review container has internet, those work fully; if it doesn't, the app cleanly falls back to the exact recovery behaviour you approved (SCN-011) — you can still save a link and fill in its details yourself, and use every other feature. All the management, search, read-later, notes, import/export, and preferences features work regardless.

### Recorded for later versions (not in this cycle, as agreed)
Automatic dead-link detection, and general visual/look-and-feel polish.

**Do you accept this software and agree to complete this cycle?** Once you confirm, I'll close out cycle 1 and record the acceptance in the session log.
